text_blocks.snippet: The COVID-19 contagion period, or the time during which an infected person can transmit the virus to others, typically lasts for several days.
According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), most people with COVID-19 are contagious from:

list.snippet: Up to 10 days: after symptoms appear

text_blocks.snippet: However, some individuals may remain contagious for longer periods, especially if they have a severe infection or underlying health conditions.
It's important to note that the contagion period can vary depending on factors such as the individual's immune system, the viral load, and the specific strain of COVID-19.
